tickets.title: A failed land can be retried
tickets.what:
Found 2026-11-22: the first live hud_land (FLOWS-04, flow fc83df390e83e1029) failed gate[3] on the known statusline-agy.test.mjs:192 flake under load 18–22. Calling hud_land again for the same job returned the stored failed flow at once (land.ts `if (prior) return prior`), so a failed land can never be retried and the caller gets a stale failure that looks like a fresh one. A second hud_land on a job whose flow is terminal and not landed starts a new run (the old record is kept or archived, not silently replaced); an active or landed flow is still returned as is. tickets.title: A hung gate test cannot stall every land
tickets.what: 2026-11-22 19:36Z: the OPTIONAL-ROLES-01 land's gate sat 45 min in `npm run test:mjs` because one child (`tests/unit/project-progress.test.mjs`, run with `--test-timeout=0`) never exited; five more lands queued behind the main-checkout lease and nothing reported. tickets.title: A follow-up send never fails the running task
tickets.what: Owner 2026-11-22: every `hud_send` or `hud_respond` to a working job makes the job's earlier MCP task end as `failed — no longer current. Use hud_read…` (src/mcp/thin-main.ts `sampleTask`, fence check ~3218; send path ~2470), so the main session sees a false failure each time it adds instructions. An addendum is not a failure. Make a follow-up to a job that already has a live task carry on that one task: re-fence the existing task to the new turn and extend its TTL, and have the send/respond return without opening a second task (or open one and end the old one silently, if the protocol allows that). The result is exactly one terminal notice per job for the chain, sent when the job reports, fails, asks or stops. Keep today's behaviour where a task really is stale: the job moved to another pane, was replaced by a repair job, or the send failed before reaching the worker. In those cases the notice says what happened, in words that do not read as a worker failure. Cover single sends, `jobs` fan-out, batch `messages`, `hud_respond`/`answers`, and the scout task.

`hud_respond` to an asking job continues the same task the same way

tickets.title: A land runner survives a rebuild of dist
tickets.what: 2026-11-22: two lands (perf-hygiene/05 flow ffc20f4c322f2231e, dogfood-fixes/16 flow f25bd7ab7d7655046) failed at `repair 1` with `The requested module './abstract-lock.js' does not provide an export named 'abstractAddress'`. Each `dist/mcp/land-runner.js` started before another land's `after: npm run build` rebuilt `dist/` with ddfdb4c8 (which added `abstractAddress` and `runner-lifetime.js`). It then lazily imported the new `runner-lifetime.js` against its cached old `abstract-lock.js`. Any long-lived HUD process that imports from `dist/` after start (land-runner, hud-mcp, hud-watch, panel) can break this way whenever a land rebuilds. Fix it so a running process never mixes builds, choosing the simplest option. Two candidates: (a) load every module eagerly at start, with no dynamic `import()` of project modules after start; or (b) run land-runner (and any other per-flow process) from an immutable snapshot of `dist/` taken at spawn, while long-lived servers restart or reload as a whole when `dist/` changes (the watcher already reloads). A failed import in a runner fails the step with a clear "HUD was rebuilt; retry the land" message and leaves the flow retryable.

acceptance.text: A test rebuilds a module that a running land-runner has not imported yet, and the flow still finishes (or fails with the retryable message, never a SyntaxError)
No dynamic import of a project module remains on the land-runner's repair path, or the runner runs from its snapshot
Targeted land tests pass

tickets.title: MCP tasks survive a server restart
tickets.what: 2026-11-22: after the owner ran `/mcp` to reconnect hud (needed to load the landed dogfood-fixes/16), Claude Code polled every outstanding task (about ten: lands, creates, sends) and each came back `Unknown or expired task`. The jobs and flows kept running, but the main session lost every completion notice and had to poll by hand. Task state lives only in the hud-mcp process (`tasks`, `activeTasks`, `landTasks` in src/mcp/thin-main.ts). Persist enough per task under `$HUD_HOME` (private files with a TTL bound): task id, job or flow id, fence, createdAt, report/attention baselines and caller. A new server process then answers `tasks/get` and `tasks/result` for tasks it did not create, by re-reading the job or flow, and delivers the same single terminal notice. Expired TTL keeps today's reply. Land tasks (flow ids) are re-read from the flow file.

tickets.title: Resuming a closed CLI tab job does not flash 'supervisor exited' and end the caller's task
tickets.what: Live 2026-11-22: hud_send to frontend-imp j8a8ba270041f7d3d (claude tab, closed after its report) resumed it as turn 2 at 05:09:59Z with a new supervisor (pid 1890832, alive) and worker (1890597, alive). The caller's MCP task nevertheless completed at once with 'waiting_orchestrator — supervisor exited; worker liveness unknown', then the job went back to working, so the main session will not be woken at turn 2's report. Cause (src/runtime/watch-runtime.ts ~575-605): the watcher read STATUS with the previous turn's supervisor pid, saw it dead, and wrote waiting_orchestrator before the new supervisor published its pid. The resume path must make the watcher ignore the old supervisor (e.g. publish the new supervisor pid / a resume marker before or atomically with the turn, or have the watcher skip a status older than the current turn's sent_at), and the caller's task must stay current until the new turn's report.
